title: Act V, Scene III

teacherSummary.text: Cassius's men are fleeing; Brutus's troops have charged too early and turned to looting. Cassius sends Titinius to see whether nearby troops are friend or foe and asks Pindarus to watch. Pindarus mistakenly reports Titinius captured. Believing all lost, Cassius has Pindarus stab him with the sword that killed Caesar: 'Caesar, thou art revenged.' Titinius returns with a victory garland from Brutus, finds Cassius dead, and kills himself. Brutus arrives, mourns Cassius as 'the last of all the Romans' and resolves to fight again.

context.history: Plutarch reports that Cassius died on his birthday, killed by his freedman Pindarus at his own command, after misreading the battle.

significance: A death built on misunderstanding: Brutus says Caesar's spirit 'turns our swords in our own proper entrails.' Note: this scene shows two suicides; preview with students.

Come hither, sirrah:

safeMessaging.teacherScript: Discuss the character's despair and what the text does with it; do not dwell on methods. Before the lesson, remind students that support is available and how to reach the counselor. Check in privately with any student who seems affected and follow your school's referral protocol.
safeMessaging.studentResource: If you or someone you know is struggling or thinking about suicide, call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, U.S.) or talk with a school counselor today.
safeMessaging.counselorPrompt: Let a counselor know in advance that this scene is being taught.
